# lazykuma

> A terminal UI for Uptime Kuma 2. Watch every monitor of every instance you
> run, live, and pause or resume them without opening the browser. Manage
> monitors, groups, tags, notification channels, maintenance (silencing),
> status pages, API keys, proxies, Docker hosts and the database, and get
> outage alerts with the terminal closed.

lazykuma is a Go TUI (terminal user interface) built with Bubble Tea /
Lip Gloss. It talks to Uptime Kuma over its Socket.IO API, which it speaks
itself over a websocket, and logs in with a username, password and optional
2FA code; only the login token is stored. It ships as a single static binary
for Linux, macOS and Windows (amd64 and arm64) with no runtime dependencies.
Uptime Kuma 1.x is detected and refused.

Besides the terminal UI it has commands that need no terminal:
`lazykuma watch` (prints every outage and raises desktop notifications until
stopped), `lazykuma autostart on|off` (starts the watch at login through a
systemd user service, XDG autostart, a macOS launch agent or the Windows Run
key), and `lazykuma status [--json]` (answers once, with exit codes for
scripts and JSON for waybar).

Typical questions this project answers: "TUI for Uptime Kuma", "Uptime Kuma
terminal client", "manage Uptime Kuma from the command line", "pause Uptime
Kuma monitors from SSH", "Uptime Kuma waybar module", "desktop notifications
for Uptime Kuma outages", "watch several Uptime Kuma instances at once",
"edit Uptime Kuma status pages without the web UI".

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/): what lazykuma does and who it is for
- [Installation](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/getting-started/installation): release binaries per OS, go install, building from source, checksums
- [Requirements](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/getting-started/requirements): Uptime Kuma 2.x, terminal, network notes
- [First run](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/getting-started/first-run): adding an instance, logging in with 2FA, menu states
- [The menu and instances](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/usage/instances): the instance screen, search, show and sort
- [Monitors, groups and tags](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/usage/monitors): create, edit, clone, delete, pause, the raw field editor
- [Monitor detail](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/usage/monitor-detail): uptime, ping chart, beats, state changes, incident timeline
- [Status pages](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/usage/status-pages): creating a page step by step, settings, sections, incidents
- [Server](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/usage/server): API keys, proxies, Docker hosts, database
- [Notification channels and silencing](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/usage/channels-and-silencing): Telegram, webhook, email, maintenance windows
- [Keys](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/usage/keys): full keybinding reference
- [lazykuma watch](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/without-the-tui/watch): outage reporting without the TUI
- [Background alerts](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/without-the-tui/background-alerts): autostart per OS, logs, troubleshooting
- [lazykuma status and waybar](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/without-the-tui/status): exit codes, JSON output, waybar module
- [config.toml](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/configuration/config-file): instances and notification settings
- [Files](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/configuration/files): config, tokens, watch lock and log, per OS
- [Changelog](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/changelog): release history
- [Contributing](https://icortesb.github.io/lazykuma-web/docs/contributing): building, testing, reporting problems

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/icortesb/lazykuma): source code, issues, releases
- [README](https://github.com/icortesb/lazykuma/blob/main/README.md): install, keys, commands, stored files
- Go module: `go install github.com/icortesb/lazykuma/cmd/lazykuma@latest` (Go 1.27+; older toolchains fetch it automatically)
